newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PT shares ignore telecoms pact.
newsitem.headline: PT shares ignore telecoms pact.

text.p: Portugal Telecom shares ignored a World Trade Organisation-sponsored telecommunications pact on Monday as the company is protected by a delay in the liberalisation of Portuguese telecommunications until 2000, analysts said.

Sixty-eight countries including Portugal agreed in Geneva on Saturday to a sweeping pact that will open up the world's $600 billion telecommunications market to competition and give a big boost to the industry and the information superhighway.
"What you'll see is a sharp drop in international tariffs by European operators," said Jose Freire, analyst with Espirito Santo Research.
"Portugal Telecom will be less affected than some others because its market is protected until 2000," he said.

Joao Vermelho, analyst with Lisbon broker Central Investimentos, said: "Everyone knew that telecommunications prices would fall. PT has the advantage of the delay in the liberalisation of Portuguese telecommunications until 2000."
Portugal Telecom shares inched higher in morning trade on Lisbon bourse, standing at 5,982 escudos, up two, in volume of 30,636 at 1130 GMT.
